title: HELIOS: A spatial omics-informed multi-organ cell atlas enables AI-based tumour microenvironment profiling and biomarker discovery from routine histopathology
summary: Spatial-omics cell identities supervise a YOLOv10-m detector for routine H&E; the study reports cross-dataset cell-classification benchmarks and cancer-cohort associations. Prognostic analyses are retrospective and do not establish clinical utility.
ai_technology: YOLOv10-m detector trained with spatial-omics-derived cell labels
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The paper reports 12.9 million cells from 60 specimens across 14 tissue types and eight cell classes; the held-out evaluation covers about 1.23 million cells, with performance varying by class. It reports cross-dataset F1 values of 0.66 (Lizard), 0.78 (MoNuSAC), and 0.59 (NuCLS), plus retrospective cancer-specific survival associations.
evidence.unknown: Methods specify five-fold train/validation/test evaluation and external benchmark comparisons. Prognostic models use retrospective TCGA-type cohorts and adjustment; authors state clinical utility remains unproven and subgroup analyses are exploratory.
evidence.ai_role: Spatial transcriptomics labels transferred to matched H&E train a multiclass YOLOv10-m cell detector; the learned operation supplies cell identity and density features for downstream analysis.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
